Yesterday, the US government announced an update to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices." A spokesperson for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) confirmed today that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum cleaner ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other well-known brands, but you can continue to use your existing products

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US, media attention focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't require legs, and the FCC's robot ban is no exception. FCC Director of Media Relations Katie Gorscak confirmed to The Verge that the ban will also cover robotic vacuum cleaners. A Roomba already in your home is not targeted by the ban, and companies can continue to import and sell approved models. However, the government claims that future foreign robots pose a national security risk, and even robotic vacuum cleaner companies have suddenly been required to commit to manufacturing in the United States.

The FCC stated that advanced robotic devices carry national security risks, and the regulations also apply to seemingly harmless products, such as robotic vacuum cleaners and automatic lawn mowers.

Unless a product is explicitly approved, or, for example, manufactured in the United States, it will not be allowed to be sold in the US.

The ban is expected to deal a particularly heavy blow to the robotic vacuum cleaner market, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own such products, you can continue to use them today — the FCC won't come to your door to confiscate your robotic vacuum cleaner.

But depending on how the ban is enforced, the robotic vacuum cleaner market may undergo drastic changes in the short term. If all this seems familiar to you, it's because the ban is very similar to the wireless router ban implemented months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robotic vacuum cleaner? Why? Feel free to tell us in the comments section.
